title: 'New World Wonder' to Be Built in the Netherlands
paragraphs: The Pyramids of Egypt and the Great Wall of China are among the most famous wonders of the world. Now, the Netherlands wants to build a new one in the city of Rotterdam.

The plan comes from an international design competition organized by Shift, a Dutch social enterprise. It asked architects to design a "new world wonder" that would make people care about the climate crisis. In July 2026, the Dutch architecture company MVRDV was named the winner. It beat several famous companies, including Heatherwick Studio, which designed the Vessel in New York.

MVRDV's design is called Rotterdam Rocks. It looks like seven giant rocks stacked on top of each other, and it will be about 30,000 square meters in size. The outside of the building will be covered with trees and plants, like a forest growing up the sides. There will also be places for soil, water and local wild animals.

Inside the "rocks," there will be exhibition spaces that look like caves. There will also be a food court, a conference center and a hotel. A path will go around the outside of the building up to a terrace on the roof, where visitors can enjoy views of the city.

The building will be on the bank of the River Maas, in a new area called Waterkant. This area will also have 3,500 environmentally friendly homes, schools and cultural spaces. The project is expected to cost 240 million euros. The designers say they will use building methods that produce less carbon.
Winy Maas, one of the founders of MVRDV, said the idea came from the need to reduce carbon dioxide emissions and create spaces for people, trees and plants.
However, there is no official opening date for the building yet.
